what_changed_recently.headline: RBI Approval for NBFC License (Airtel Money Limited)
what_changed_recently.detail: Airtel's subsidiary, Airtel Money Limited, received RBI approval on February 13, 2026, to operate as a Type II non-deposit-taking NBFC, allowing Airtel to launch direct lending digital financial services.

what_changed_recently.headline: Expansion of Data Centre Capacity to 1 GW
what_changed_recently.detail: Airtel announced a large-scale expansion plan for its data centre business (Nxtra) to build 1 GW of capacity over the coming years, securing key land parcels in Mumbai and stitching contracts with hyperscalers.

what_changed_recently.headline: Increase in Stake in Airtel Africa to Over 79%
what_changed_recently.detail: Airtel completed an EPS-accretive share swap transaction during Q1 FY27, increasing its equity stake in the Africa business to over 79%.

what_changed_recently.headline: Tightening FWA Acquisition Quality and Pivot to Fiber
what_changed_recently.detail: Due to high churn from aggressive low entry pricing and global chipset/memory price inflation, Airtel tightened acquisition parameters on Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) and re-pivoted primary expansion back to fiber.

growth_drivers.description: Scaling Nxtra data centre capacity from 120-130 MW to 1 GW over the coming years by acquiring prime land in Mumbai and securing anchor contracts with hyperscalers like Google.
growth_drivers.execution_status: Land acquisition in progress and landmark deals being finalized
growth_drivers.expected_impact: Expand market share significantly beyond the current 12% in India's fast-growing data centre market.
growth_drivers.source_quote: We are working towards our ambition to build one gigawatt in the next few years.

growth_drivers.driver_title: NBFC Digital Financial Services & Airtel Finance Storefront
growth_drivers.description: Launching direct lending services via the newly licensed NBFC (Airtel Money Ltd) integrated with Airtel Payments Bank on the Airtel Finance storefront.
growth_drivers.execution_status: Went live within 9 months of license application; monthly disbursements reached ₹750+ Cr.
growth_drivers.expected_impact: Build a meaningful new growth engine leveraging Airtel's large customer base with lower customer acquisition and collection costs.
growth_drivers.source_quote: We recently went live with our lending services, marking an important milestone in our financial services journey.

growth_drivers.description: Built-in-India sovereign telco-grade cloud platform designed to meet cloud migration needs for enterprises, PSUs, and regulated industries.
growth_drivers.execution_status: MeitY certified; onboarded 11 new customers in Q1 FY27 taking total to 33.
growth_drivers.expected_impact: Capture growing enterprise demand as business needs move beyond core connectivity into digital and cloud solutions.
growth_drivers.source_quote: Over the quarter, we have added 11 new customers, taking the total customer count to 33.

promise_vs_delivery.management_promise: Drive portfolio premiumisation and quality customer acquisition to achieve industry-leading ARPU growth (ARPU was ₹245 in FY25).
promise_vs_delivery.promise_quote: Attracting and retaining high-value customers remains the cornerstone of our strategy. We have achieved an industry-leading ARPU of C245
promise_vs_delivery.actual_outcome: ARPU expanded further to ₹257 in FY26 and reached ₹264 in Q1 FY27, driven by 4G/5G upgrades, data consumption, and postpaid growth.
promise_vs_delivery.actual_quote: The Company’s focus on portfolio premiumisation and high-quality customer acquisition continued to support industry-leading ARPU, which rose to ₹257 from ₹245
promise_vs_delivery.stocker_analysis: Target delivered cleanly. ARPU grew from ₹245 in FY25 to ₹257 in FY26 and ₹264 in Q1 FY27, supported by record postpaid additions (1M in Q1 FY27) and 5G Fast Lane adoption.

promise_vs_delivery.management_promise: Deleverage balance sheet through strong cash generation and spectrum debt prepayments (Net Debt to EBITDAaL ratio was 2.1x standalone / 1.5x consolidated in FY25).
promise_vs_delivery.promise_quote: Strong cash generation supports balance sheet deleveraging and a step-up in dividends.
promise_vs_delivery.actual_outcome: Net Debt to EBITDAaL ratio improved to 1.3x standalone / 0.8x consolidated at end of FY26 and reached 0.7x in Q1 FY27, prompting credit rating upgrades to AAA (CRISIL/CARE) and Baa2 (Moody's).
promise_vs_delivery.actual_quote: improving Net Debt to EBITDAaL ratio to 1.3x at end of March 2026 vs 2.1x at the end of March 2025.
promise_vs_delivery.stocker_analysis: Prepaid high-cost DoT liabilities and external debt, reducing consolidated net debt to EBITDAaL to 0.8x in FY26 and 0.7x in Q1 FY27.

promise_vs_delivery.area: EBITDAaL Margin Expansion via War on Waste
promise_vs_delivery.management_promise: Sustain cost optimisation through 'War on Waste' program to deliver margin expansion (standalone EBITDAaL margin was 49.0% in FY25).
promise_vs_delivery.promise_quote: Our ‘War on Waste’ program yielded strong outcomes, resulting in substantial savings and contributing to a healthy improvement in EBITDAaL margins
promise_vs_delivery.actual_outcome: Standalone EBITDAaL margin expanded to 51.4% in FY26 (up 240 bps YoY), with consolidated EBITDAaL margin standing at 51.2% in FY26 and 51.0% in Q1 FY27.
promise_vs_delivery.actual_quote: sustained margin expansion, EBITDAaL margins in FY 2025-26 improved to 51.4% as compared to 49.0% in previous year.
promise_vs_delivery.stocker_analysis: War on Waste program achieved structural cost resets, lifting standalone EBITDAaL margin by 240 bps YoY to 51.4%.

demand_momentum.summary: Robust demand across mobile data upgrades, postpaid migration, home broadband, digital enterprise services, and financial services in India and Africa.

segment_trends.trend: +11.5% standalone revenue growth in FY26; ARPU expanded to ₹264 in Q1 FY27 with record 1M postpaid net additions.
+31.7% YoY revenue growth in FY26; record 4.2M customer additions in FY26 reaching 14.2M total subs.
+24.0% constant currency revenue growth and +30.5% EBITDA growth in FY26.
Digital business revenue grew 27% in FY26; Nxtra Data Centre revenue up 17.2%.

demand_momentum.market_share_and_pricing: Achieved lifetime high revenue market share in India mobile. ARPU expanded to ₹264. Management stresses that longer-term pricing architecture requires repair by charging for data usage.
headwinds_and_risks: FWA churn from aggressive low acquisition pricing combined with global memory and chipset cost inflation.
Macro uncertainty and FX volatility in Africa (e.g. Nigerian Naira devaluation).
Geopolitical friction in West Asia temporarily affecting international roaming revenue.
demand_momentum.source_quote: Growth was driven by continued expansion in customer base, higher data consumption, portfolio premiumization and rapidly growing digital portfolio.

risks_and_cash.working_capital_and_receivables: Standalone trade receivables decreased to ₹28,935 Mn as of March 31, 2026 (from ₹31,715 Mn as of March 31, 2025). Consolidated trade receivables stood at ₹79,776 Mn. Expected credit loss matrix is continuously applied based on historical credit performance.
risks_and_cash.debt_and_capex_burden: Consolidated net debt (excluding leases) declined significantly to ₹910,485 Mn (March 31, 2026) from ₹1,385,086 Mn in FY25. Consolidated Net Debt to EBITDAaL ratio improved to 0.8x in FY26 and 0.7x in Q1 FY27. FY26 consolidated Capex was ₹475,218 Mn (Q1 FY27 capex was ₹13,390 Cr).
risks_and_cash.margin_and_cost_pressures: Input cost pressures managed via War on Waste program, including elimination of diesel dependence through solarization of ~42,000 sites and AI-led operational efficiency.
execution_and_bottlenecks: Rising global memory and chipset costs impacting FWA hardware economics.
Potential last-mile IT connectivity failures and software upgrade integration risks in developing African regions.
regulatory_or_legal_headwinds: Escalating spectrum prices, subscriber verification norms, and data privacy regulations.
Sub-judice legal and tax disputes (standalone provisions towards sub-judice matters stood at ₹287,918 Mn as of March 31, 2026).
risks_and_cash.source_quote: On a reported basis, net debt declined by H300,305 million year-on-year, improving Net Debt to EBITDAaL ratio to 1.3x at end of March 2026 vs 2.1x

positive_triggers: Monetization and buildout of 1 GW Nxtra data centre capacity.
Scale-up of NBFC digital lending via Airtel Money Ltd and Airtel Finance storefront.
Upcoming London listing of Airtel Money (Africa) planned in H2 2026.
Potential tariff architecture repair charging for incremental data consumption.
main_risks: Foreign exchange devaluation risks and currency controls across African markets.
Legal and regulatory contingencies related to sub-judice levies and AGR liabilities.
Global memory/chipset price inflation impacting hardware deployment costs.
what_to_watch_next: Progress and timeline on the Airtel Money London IPO in H2 2026.
Net additions momentum in home broadband following the pivot from FWA to FTTH.
Adoption rate of 5G Standalone Fast Lane postpaid plans.
stocker_view.investor_summary: Bharti Airtel demonstrates high operational discipline, gaining lifetime-high revenue market share and expanding mobile ARPU to ₹264 in Q1 FY27. EBITDAaL margins expanded to 51.4% standalone, driven by the 'War on Waste' program. Disciplined cash flow generation and debt prepayments reduced consolidated Net Debt to EBITDAaL to 0.7x, resulting in credit rating upgrades to AAA/Baa2. Strategic capital allocation into growth adjacencies—1 GW data centre expansion, sovereign cloud, NBFC lending rollout, and the upcoming London listing of Airtel Money—positions Airtel strongly for sustained earnings compounding.
